retry: Retries are appropriate for transient failures when operations are safe to repeat and attempts are bounded.
backoff: Exponential backoff increases the delay between retries. Jitter reduces synchronized retry storms.
timeout: Timeouts bound how long a dependency attempt may consume resources. Overall request deadlines bound the complete request.
circuit-breaker: Circuit breakers stop repeated calls to an unhealthy dependency, then probe recovery after a cooldown.
fallback: Fallback providers can preserve availability, but degraded responses should be observable and explicitly marked.
cache: Fresh caches reduce latency and dependency load. Stale-if-error can preserve partial availability during outages.
rate-limit: Rate limiting protects shared capacity and prevents one caller from exhausting the service.
observability: Structured logs, trace IDs, metrics, and health checks make failures diagnosable.
budget: Attempt, token, and cost budgets bound resource consumption even when retries and fallbacks are enabled.
graceful-degradation: Graceful degradation returns a bounded, explicit degraded result instead of crashing or inventing success.
